Thanks again for the demo last week — ClearPath is ready to move forward on renewal. We're planning to renew and increase committed capacity to support a larger inference footprint (roughly 2x current monthly tokens, see attached estimates). We'd like to: 

- Move to an 18-month term starting 2027-06-01
- Add an order form for the additional capacity and burst pool
- Submit some redlines to the MSA (attached) — a handful of changes around indemnity, data retention, and an SLA credit cap

I've attached: CPS_proposed_orderform_v3.docx and CPS_redlines_MSA_v2.docx. Amy (legal) and Procurement are copied. Can you confirm next steps and timeline for internal review? Ideally we'd have counters and a DocuSign-ready orderform within two weeks.

Appreciate it — El

Plan:
1) Legal (David) will triage the MSA redlines and call out anything high-risk.
2) Ops/CS (Jordan) will confirm the capacity numbers and propose an orderform layout that supports burst capacity and a short ramp schedule.
3) I'll coordinate commercial (term/price) and aim to present a consolidated counter by end of next week (target 2027-04-18).

Couple quick clarifying Qs for Procurement:
- Can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly tokens and peak burst multiplier you want us to guarantee in the orderform? (Elena mentioned ~2x overall, but we need a concrete baseline for pricing.)

David/Jordan/Irene — looping you in; your guidance on indemnity/data retention language and whether a shorter term (12 vs 18 months) would be acceptable commercially is helpful.

Subject: Re: Renewal + Capacity Increase — Contract Redlines

Hi team — I reviewed CPS_redlines_MSA_v2.docx and flagged the high-level items. Attached is a short summary PDF with suggested Redwood-friendly alternatives (redline_notes_from_redwood_legal.pdf). Top items to resolve: 

1) Indemnity carveout: ClearPath requested removal of Redwood's limitation for third-party claims tied to customer data. We can offer a narrow carveout for gross negligence/willful misconduct, but cannot accept open-ended indemnity. Proposed compromise in the PDF.

2) Data retention & deletion: need to add explicit customer instructions and a 90-day post-termination retrieval window; Redwood cannot store customer data beyond agreed retention without written approval. Proposed language added.

3) SLA credit cap: current ask would allow credits up to 100% of fees; suggest a cap of 50% and a cure period. Also recommend a reporting cadence and measurable metrics in Exhibit B.

4) Audit rights: Amy requested broad audit rights. We're open to providing SOC2 evidence and scoped audit cooperation but push back on on-site vendor audits for production lanes.

Next steps: if ClearPath accepts the three compromises above, we can produce a clean counter-MSA and a draft orderform to attach to DocuSign. Hannah — please confirm commercial side (term length, pricing) and Jordan to confirm capacity numbers so I can tailor Exhibit B.

Attachment: redline_notes_from_redwood_legal.pdf (summary of legal positions).

Thanks — David
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
From: Elena Marsh <emarsh@clearpathsys.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Amy Lin <amy.lin@clearpathsys.com>, Procurement <procurement@clearpathsys.com>, david_kim@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + Capacity Increase — Contract Redlines

Hannah/David — thanks for the quick turnaround and the helpful summary. A few updates from our side: 

- Procurement confirmed they will issue a PO (attached PO_30421.pdf) once the final orderform is ready. They prefer DocuSign flow for signature.
- On term: internal stakeholders pushed back on 18 months; they prefer 12 months (+ an option to extend with a 30-day notice). Pricing impact is acceptable to them. Can Redwood produce a 12-month counter with an optional 6-month extension clause?
- We accept Redwood's recommended approach on indemnity language (narrow carveout) and the SLA credit cap at 50%, provided we get clear Exhibit B metrics.
- Audit: SOC2 report and log-export cooperation is sufficient for now; no on-site audits required.

Next asks for Redwood:
1) Final counter-MSA (with the three compromises David summarized)
2) Draft orderform that includes: baseline tokens, peak burst multiplier (x2), ramp schedule, and pricing line-items
3) DocuSign envelope for the orderform + MSA when ready

We'll aim to return the signed PO within 3 business days of receiving DocuSign. If you can get a clean counter and orderform to us by Monday 2027-05-03, that would be ideal.

Thanks — El
